authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: An intimate documentary music photograph of a small live band making music together at the first quiet downbeat of an afternoon stage rehearsal. The reference-guided lead musician is a fictional adult woman; use the supplied image for visible face and hair guidance. Preserve a softly tapered oval face, dark rounded almond eyes, gently arched straight brows, a small softly rounded nose, and softly full natural pink lips, and a chin-length straight dark bob with a loose central part and fine wispy strands over the forehead. Her expression combines focused listening with a small, unguarded smile, natural skin texture and warm presence. She wears a loosely tucked cream cotton shirt with sleeves rolled to the forearms, dark straight trousers and worn low shoes. The lead stands center-left with both feet planted on the wooden stage, her whole body occupying roughly seventy percent of the image height. A broad shoulder strap supports a compact red electric guitar against the front of her hips. Her left fingertips press separate strings onto the frets at the middle of the neck, with her thumb behind the neck; her right thumb and index finger hold a small pick that visibly touches the strings above the pickups. Both wrists, the entire neck and headstock, the bridge, and both shoe soles remain readable. Her small downward head nod toward the drummer carries the count-in, her lips just parting with the breath of the cue. The drummer at frame-right answers that nod with one stick meeting the snare head while the other stays raised separately; the seated drummer's knees and stool support read through the open space below the drum. A bassist behind the lead at frame-left turns toward the same cue, the bass held diagonally clear of the lead's arms, with one hand around its neck and the other poised above its strings. Their converging attention makes the first beat feel shared rather than posed for an audience. A single cable plugs into the lead guitar's visible output jack, falls in a loose arc to the floor, and follows a continuous visible route to the front input socket of a small amplifier at the lower right; separate space surrounds each plug. Sparse rehearsal equipment, a low wedge monitor and the edge of the empty club floor establish a small working stage. A broad high window sends soft late-afternoon side light across faces and hands, balanced by one dim amber stage practical. Use a landscape three-by-two frame, a natural forty-millimeter perspective at chest height and enough depth of field to hold the lead's face, both operating hands and the two bandmates in readable detail. Keep the lead's face near frontal with only a slight turn toward the drummer; place the drummer close enough laterally for the reciprocal cue and snare contact to remain visible. The main impression is the fragile pleasure of three people finding their first shared beat.
